 Order

As prayed by the counsel for the appellant, the service of notice on respondent no.2 is dispensed with at the risk and cost of the appellant Heard on IA No.6294/2023, an application for condonation of delay.
The application is opposed by the counsel for the respondent no1.
For the reasons stated in the application, same is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
With consent, heard finally.

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 08.12.2022 passed by 25th MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.3050/2018 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the Bhuraibai, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,74,500/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.4,09,500/-
 (i.e.Rs.4200 x 12 25% FP=63000 x 13 - 1/2 PE)
 Consortium -Rs.1,32,000/

Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 ---------------------

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

He further submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.4200/- per month which is on the lower side considering the minimum wages prescribed even for an unskilled labour.
Hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation.

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, even if there was no proof of income, the same ought to have been assessed on the basis of the minimum wages applicable to an unskilled labour prescribed for the relevant period.

In view of the above, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the lower side which is modified as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.6,82,500/-
 (i.e.Rs.7000 x 12 25% FP x 13 - 1/2 PE)
 Consortium -Rs.1,32,000/-

Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 ------------------
. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.8,47,500/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.5,74,500/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,73,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,73,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
